findings.source_passage: For that particular form of mental trouble an eminent physician recommends unlimited Hors d'œuvre, Lobster à l'américane, Chicken Newberg, and Pêche Melba! Let's go and get them!
findings.source_locator: after 'I have come into money' exchange
findings.why_it_matters: The final 'Let's go and get them!' is Tuppence's voice-defining exclamatory energy; the draft cuts it, flattening the comic momentum that defines her register in this scene.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Let's go and get them!' as the closing punch of Tuppence's speech.

findings.source_passage: Great Jehosaphat! My dear girl, don't wave Fishers aloft like that! They're not Fishers. They're five times better than Fishers, and this one's ten times better!
findings.source_locator: after 'Oh, unbelieving one!' up to 'Even so, O King'
findings.why_it_matters: The 'Fishers'/'five times better'/'ten times better' exchange is a voice-establishing comic riff that conveys period flavour and the pair's banter; collapsing it to 'Bank-notes fluttered. Tommy blinked' erases a distinctive Christie comedic beat.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least the 'Jehosaphat / not Fishers / five times better' exchange verbatim or near-verbatim before 'Even so, O King.'

findings.source_passage: I must have been drinking unawares! Am I dreaming, Tuppence, or do I really behold a large quantity of five-pound notes being waved about in a dangerous fashion?
findings.source_locator: Tommy's speech just before 'Even so, O King'
findings.why_it_matters: The draft keeps only 'Am I dreaming…' half, dropping 'I must have been drinking unawares!' — a comic hyperbolic phrase that is part of the signature voice rhythm of Tommy's mock-astonishment and the scene's comic tone.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the opening clause 'I must have been drinking unawares!' to Tommy's speech.

findings.source_passage: You have made rather a hog of yourself! So have I for that matter, but I flatter myself that my choice of dishes was more judicious than yours.
findings.source_locator: after 'Oh, dear, what a lot I have eaten!' before ordering coffee
findings.why_it_matters: This self-deflating, mock-pompous exchange is distinctive Christie banter; erasing it strips the post-meal beat of its voice and collapses what the source uses as a tonal breathing space before the plot resumes.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the exchange about 'hog of yourself' and 'judicious choice of dishes' before the coffee order.

findings.source_passage: 'Shades of Pelmanism!' said Tommy, and relapsed into silence.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a small but textually distinctive period idiom and character voice marker — the kind of throwaway that anchors the novel in its era and in Tommy's comic persona. Its loss is typical of middle-scene compression erasing period register.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Tommy's 'Shades of Pelmanism!' quip as a one-liner before the thinking pause.

findings.source_passage: The day passed pleasantly. The evening even more so. Two of the five-pound notes were now irretrievably dead.
findings.why_it_matters: The draft reduces 'irretrievably dead' to 'died gallantly' — a paraphrase that loses the dry, deadpan finality of Christie's exact wording, which is a minor but characteristic stylistic touch.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the verbatim closing: 'Two of the five-pound notes were now irretrievably dead.'

summary: The draft preserves plot and key dialogue but systematically erases the middle-scene comic banter (Fishers exchange, 'drinking unawares', 'hog of yourself', 'Shades of Pelmanism') that carries Christie's voice-establishing signature in this segment, producing four medium-severity losses that together trigger regeneration.
